images.text: Exploring space shouldn't be a dream that is  “out of this world”. Ever since the advent of rockets, space exploration has taken new dimensions. Man is on a mission to discover the millions of  galaxies and planets,  of which the world beyond ours is comprised . While the study of space is carried out by astronomers, the actual physical exploration is conducted by both unmanned robotic probes and human spaceflight.  The advancement of rocket technology, whose development occurred in the early 20th century, propelled space exploration to new heights.

The subject of space exploration has been picking up speed over the past few years. One reason could be that many people are concerned about our own survival as a species. With all the wars, famine, and pollution, it is likely life on Earth won't survive . So, to preserve human existence, scientists have developed theories of how humans can live on a different planet. It's a tall order that requires ongoing research and exploration.  Many of the world's rich such as Elon Musk, whose investments of billions of dollars into his own SpaceX company, strongly believes that there will be a similar world outside ours that has the potential to save our species. SpaceX ,which is one of the first privately owned companies, has been deeply involved in space exploration. They continue to find ways to reduce exploration and transportation costs in order to make the colonization of Mars a reality.
With the rapid rate of technological advancement in space exploration, it is possible that we will be packing our bags for Mars in the very near future.

Will, Won't, Should, Shouldn't, Can to Speculate about the Present
You can use modal verbs like should, shouldn't and can to speculate about a present situation.

Use will or won't when you are completely certain about something.
With all the wars, famine, and pollution, it is likely* life on Earth won't survive.
*Here the word likely means that the speaker feels that the event will certainly happen.

Use should or shouldn't when you assume that something is probably true because everything happens as expected.
In negative events, however, will is more commonly used.
A plane ticket will cost more during peak season. (instead of “should cost more”)

Use can to talk about general possibilities. For a more specific situation, use could.
Compare the following sentences:
Shopping online can put you at risk for identity theft.
My sister could be shopping right now because Christmas is next week.
Exploring space shouldn't be a dream that is “out of this world”.
One reason could be that many people are concerned about our own survival as a species.
Elon Musk strongly believes that we will discover a similar world outside ours.
You already use many different verbs in your sentences. However, some verbs are followed by prepositions.
If you want to make relative clauses with these verbs, there are certain rules you need to remember. Look at the structure of the sentences below.

Prepositions are used only before the object relative pronouns whom or which. They are never used before who or that.
If you put the preposition after the verb, then you can use who, whom, which or that.
You can even omit the preposition and the sentence meaning will be the same.

WHOSE
You use whose in relative clauses to show possession. It cannot be left out of the relative clause.

I know a woman whose son was in the army.
The house whose faucets are made of gold is for sale.
